build: Early Access; last update "Small maintenance update" 2023-07-06 (chapters 10-11 on 2023-01-20)

package.basis: Desk only: Steam store/appdetails, 441 English Steam reviews via the review API, Steam news, a Steam discussion thread and prior repo research; not played.

fun.source: desk estimate: praised pacing and clean queue planning (85.1% of 1,043 English reviews positive), but negative reviews cite repetition, few decisions and 20-30 min check-ins; below Loop Hero 74.0 and near Melvor 65.4 on idle-hybrid; promising band.

evidence.quote: Increlution is a minimalistic incremental game about time management
The graphics are very clean and the story is captivating

dims.note: Clean text-and-icon UI; no illustrations (one reviewer asks for them).

evidence.quote: watching bars fill up and repeat
the user interface is extremely clean and surprisingly powerful
Balanced, clear UI
Simple intuitive user interface and automation system.

dims.note: Three agreeing reviews; the post-death screen shows progress clearly.

evidence.quote: the game has the option to make a sound to tell you to come back when it needs you

dims.note: Only a notification sound is mentioned; not listened.

evidence.quote: Using the step-by-step queue system, you can plan exactly what you want to happen and the game will automatically follow your orders.
players asked for automation "after 1 or 2 completions rather than 10" (prior research)
Start a run, wait a bit (15m+) - Click a button or two, wait a minute

dims.note: Core act in minute one and a death/reset within ~30 min, but per-action automation takes 10 completions (later lowered for some).

evidence.quote: the pacing is perfect. There was never a run where I didn't feel like the tension was absolutely dialed in.
Beyond the first chapter, the game is pure repetition with increasingly longer time increments
Do this 500 times before it can be automated

dims.note: Rubric anchor is ~80; desk evidence is split, so 68 (within the 15-point tolerance). No ending: the story stops at chapter 11 for a ~220-250 h playthrough.

evidence.quote: you also get to decide the order of doing things in depth opening up for a lot of min maxing
There is a tiny sprinkle of strategy and 'builds' as you get near the end
There are few, if any, real decisions to make.

dims.note: Queue order is the build; one optimal route per chapter.

evidence.quote: price S$4.25 (one purchase); no DLC; not free to play
There are no microtransactions or any of the other nonsense that plagues the genre
There is basically no offline progress since you need to come back every 20-30 minutes

dims.note: One fair price, no IAP; but the queue pauses when empty, so absence earns nothing after a life ends.

evidence.quote: You get to slowly watch as things that originally take 20 minutes slowly take less and less time

dims.note: Speed-up across lives is the payoff; little audiovisual feedback.

evidence.quote: Zero bugs.
Small maintenance update (2023-07-06): render-buffer fix after minimizing on some Windows systems

dims.note: Stable; but an Early Access build without updates since 2023.

evidence.quote: near the end of the 220-250 hour game
Game is terminally in EA ... the story is incomplete and probably will never be finished.
4+ years since update, it's obvious it is no longer being worked on

dims.note: A long but repetitive 11-chapter story without an ending; development stalled.

evidence.quote: takes inspiration from roguelite games ... Every generation has a better chance at survival
an actually unique one versus the cookie cutter ones

dims.note: A legible, distinctive pitch (life-as-a-run incremental); the screenshot is text.

evidence.quote: platforms: Windows, Mac, Linux; supported_languages: 'English'; categories: Steam Cloud

dims.note: Steam only (three desktop OSes, cloud save); no web or mobile; English only.

learn.practice: Show per-run improvement against the previous life at each stage, so every death reads as progress.
learn.evidence: https://steamcommunity.com/profiles/76561198023131329/recommended/1593350/ "you get to see howmuch seconds you were faster then last run at each stage"

learn.practice: A post-death screen plus an exploration tracker that make cross-run progress undeniable (maps directly to Idlever's death screen and report).
learn.evidence: https://steamcommunity.com/profiles/76561198042171166/recommended/1593350/ "The post-death screen and exploration tracker provide clear evidence that you continue to progress each iteration"

learn.practice: Do not make offline stop at an unautomated chore: Increlution's pause-when-empty queue is the most-cited respect complaint; keep offline uncapped after the scout.
learn.evidence: https://steamcommunity.com/profiles/76561198934151557/recommended/1593350/ "There is basically no offline progress since you need to come back every 20-30 minutes"

learn.practice: Ship an ending, or the long tail sours: abandoned Early Access with an unfinished story is the core of the negative reviews.
learn.evidence: https://steamcommunity.com/profiles/76561198005869901/recommended/1593350/ "the story is incomplete and probably will never be finished"
